title: ISACA Certified in the Governance of Enterprise IT (CGEIT)
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the ISACA CGEIT exam content outline (four domains and weights). Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: A corporate board wants assurance that technology delivers value and that its risks are managed. Which statement best defines enterprise governance of IT?
options: The board and executive management direct and control IT by evaluating, directing and monitoring
The IT department alone owns the policies, standards and procedures used to operate technology
The external auditor sets the IT strategy and holds management accountable for its execution
The vendor community collectively decides the enterprise architecture and the technology roadmap
items.explanation: Enterprise governance of IT is the responsibility of the board and executive management, who evaluate needs, set direction and monitor outcomes. Delegating it to the IT department, an auditor or vendors removes the accountability that governance exists to place at the top.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A large organization is applying COBIT and must distinguish governance from management. Which activity belongs to the governance domain?
options: Planning, building and running solutions within agreed constraints
Building and configuring the applications that run the business
Running the daily IT operations and resolving incidents
Evaluating stakeholder needs and setting the direction for IT
items.explanation: COBIT places evaluate, direct and monitor in the governance domain and plan, build, run and monitor in management. Board-level evaluation and direction of IT is governance, whereas building, running and delivering solutions is management.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: An enterprise is tailormaking COBIT to its own context. Which input most directly determines how the governance system should be designed?
options: The license count and version of the framework that the vendor recommends
The seniority of the staff who will operate the governance processes
The enterprise goals, risk profile, size, culture and regulatory environment
The number of servers and endpoints currently deployed across the estate
items.explanation: COBIT design factors are the enterprise-specific context such as goals, risk profile, threat landscape, size, culture and compliance obligations. Hardware counts, license tiers and staff seniority are not the design factors that shape a governance system.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A governance committee is reviewing candidate frameworks to direct and control IT. Which statement best captures the purpose of adopting such a framework?
options: To guarantee that no audit finding will ever be raised against the IT function
To replace all internal policies with a single external vendor document
To provide a structured set of practices that can be tailored to govern and manage IT
To certify the enterprise against a standard and remove the need for judgment
items.explanation: A framework supplies structure and good practices that must be tailored; it is not a guarantee of clean audits, it complements rather than replaces internal policy, and it never removes the need for professional judgment.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: An enterprise has adopted a recognized IT governance framework but stakeholders report it is unused. Which action best addresses the root cause?
options: Add more framework processes until every published objective is covered in full
Map the framework to the enterprise objectives and assign clear ownership of each practice
Commission an external audit to publicly report the low adoption rate
Purchase the premium tooling suite that the framework publisher sells
items.explanation: Low uptake usually reflects a framework imposed without localization, ownership or relevance to enterprise goals. Mapping practices to real objectives with named owners makes them usable, whereas adding volume or buying tools does not address the mismatch.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A practitioner is assessing whether an IT governance system covers all necessary enablers. Which set best describes the COBIT governance system components?
options: Processes, organizational structures, principles and policies, information, culture, people and skills, services and infrastructure, and applications
Audit findings, remediation plans, exceptions and waivers only
Hardware, software, networks, data centers and cloud subscriptions only
Budgets, purchase orders, invoices, contracts and vendor records only
items.explanation: COBIT describes the governance system through several enabler categories including processes, structures, principles and policies, information, culture, people and skills, services and infrastructure, and applications. Lists confined to assets, procurement or audit artifacts are incomplete.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A board asks how mature its IT governance is compared with peers. Which approach best supports an objective maturity assessment?
options: Count the number of policies that exist in the document repository
Compare the IT budget as a proportion of total enterprise revenue
Ask the IT manager to estimate a single percentage for overall governance
Rate the governance practices against defined capability levels using consistent evidence
items.explanation: Maturity is rated against defined capability levels with evidence for each practice, which makes the result repeatable and comparable. A self-estimated percentage, a document count or a budget ratio each measures something else and cannot stand in for a capability assessment.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A board is applying the ISO IEC 38500 standard for the governance of IT and wants technology to be fit for purpose and used well now and in the foreseeable future. Which governance principle best matches this expectation?
options: Acquisition
Conformance
Human behaviour
Performance
items.explanation: ISO IEC 38500 sets out principles including responsibility, strategy, acquisition, performance, conformance and human behaviour. Performance requires IT to be fit for purpose and used well now and in the future, whereas the other principles address procurement, compliance with obligations and the way people act.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: An executive committee is cascading enterprise goals into IT goals. Which outcome best demonstrates a well-cascaded governance system?
options: Each IT goal is written by the IT department without reference to the business
Each IT goal duplicates the enterprise goal using identical wording
Each IT goal is traceable to the enterprise goals and risks it is meant to support
Each IT goal is set only after the annual budget is fully spent
items.explanation: Cascading requires an explicit, traceable link from enterprise goals and risks to the IT goals and enablers that support them. Goals written in isolation, merely duplicated, or timed to budget exhaustion are not alignment.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A board wants to delegate operational oversight of IT without losing accountability. Which arrangement best reflects sound governance?
options: A steering committee with a clear mandate and delegated decision rights reporting to the board
An external vendor who chairs the committee and approves its own work
An informal group of volunteers who meet only when an incident occurs
A single IT manager who makes all technology decisions without oversight
items.explanation: Delegation works when the board grants a defined mandate and decision rights and receives reporting in return. Unstructured groups, unaccountable individuals and self-approving vendors do not preserve the board accountability.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: An enterprise is updating its IT strategic plan. Which characteristic indicates the plan is aligned with the business strategy?
options: It is written entirely by the technology vendor that supplies the platform
It is kept confidential from business leaders to protect competitive information
It lists only the hardware and software the IT department wants to buy
It states IT objectives that clearly support the stated enterprise goals and outcomes
items.explanation: An IT strategy aligns when it expresses how technology will enable the specific enterprise goals and outcomes. A shopping list, a vendor-authored document or a plan hidden from business leaders cannot demonstrate that linkage.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A CIO must show that the IT roadmap supports business priorities. Which artifact most directly provides that evidence?
options: An inventory of every server serial number in the data center
A list of open help-desk tickets by priority over the last quarter
A strategy map that links IT initiatives to enterprise objectives and measures
A copy of the vendor product release notes for the coming year
items.explanation: A strategy map makes the cause-and-effect relationship between IT initiatives and enterprise objectives explicit and measurable. Asset inventories, incident volumes and vendor roadmaps describe activity, not alignment to business priorities.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: Business leaders complain that IT solutions do not meet their needs. Which governance practice best improves this engagement?
options: Having IT approve its own requirements without any business involvement
Involving business stakeholders in defining and prioritizing IT demand from the outset
Freezing requirements at the start and refusing any later clarification
Deferring all business input until after implementation is complete
items.explanation: Shared ownership of demand definition and prioritization aligns solutions with business need. IT-authored requirements, frozen and uninformed specifications, and post hoc input all exclude the business from the decisions that determine whether value is delivered.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: An enterprise wants technology decisions to support a coherent target state rather than accumulate point solutions. Which discipline best supports this goal?
options: A practice of replacing the core platform with every new vendor offering
A policy that requires every department to purchase the cheapest available tool
A rule that all projects must use the same programming language indefinitely
Enterprise architecture that describes current, target and transition states with governing principles
items.explanation: Enterprise architecture provides the current, target and transition views plus principles that keep investments coherent. Cost minimization, language mandates and perpetual replacement are not architecture disciplines and do not produce a target state.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: An enterprise is pursuing a digital transformation program. Which governance action is most important at the outset?
options: Suspending all risk reporting until the program is complete
Buying the newest tools before defining the intended outcomes
Establishing clear accountability and decision rights for the transformation outcomes
Delegating the entire program to a single technology supplier
items.explanation: Transformations fail most often for governance reasons, so accountability, decision rights and outcome ownership must be set first. Outsourcing ownership, silencing risk reporting or purchasing ahead of defining outcomes inverts sound governance.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A governance board must decide among competing IT investments. Which basis best reflects disciplined prioritization?
options: The size of the department that submitted the largest funding request
Alignment with strategy and expected value relative to risk and cost
The order in which requests arrived in the email inbox
The vendor that offers the largest discount during the quarter
items.explanation: Prioritization compares each investment strategic contribution and expected value against its risk and cost. Submission size, arrival order and vendor discounts are not decision criteria that advance the enterprise goals.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: The board asks how to govern adoption of an emerging technology with unsettled standards. Which response is most appropriate?
options: Run a controlled pilot with defined evaluation criteria and a staged decision gate
Deploy it enterprise-wide immediately to gain first-mover advantage
Reject it permanently because standards are not yet mature
Let individual staff adopt it freely without any oversight
items.explanation: Uncertain technologies are best governed through bounded experimentation with explicit criteria and a gate that decides whether to scale, adjust or stop. Instant enterprise rollout, blanket rejection and unmanaged adoption all forgo the evidence a controlled pilot provides.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A governance team wants to raise IT from an operational supplier to a strategic partner. Which shift best reflects that maturity increase?
options: IT centralizes all decisions so that business units have no input
IT takes orders more quickly while leaving strategy entirely to the business
Business and IT jointly own strategy and value decisions rather than IT merely taking orders
IT reduces its contact with business units to avoid competing priorities
items.explanation: Strategic partnership means shared ownership of strategy and value between business and IT. Faster order-taking, reduced engagement and centralization all keep IT in a service-execution role rather than elevating it to a partner.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: An enterprise is redesigning how IT services are delivered across business units. Which element defines the target operating model?
options: The current org chart with no changes to roles or reporting lines
The future blueprint for capabilities, processes, organization and technology
The schedule of vendor contract renewals for the coming year
The list of applications that will be retired at the next fiscal year end
items.explanation: A target operating model is the future-state blueprint covering capabilities, processes, organization and enabling technology. Retirement lists, unchanged org charts and contract schedules describe narrow or present-state artifacts, not a target design.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A newly formed IT governance council needs a clear charter. Which content is most essential to that charter?
options: The biographies of every member and their previous employers
The marketing plan for the enterprise products and services
The detailed test scripts for applications under development
Its decision rights, membership, mandate and reporting obligations
items.explanation: A governance charter defines what the body decides, who sits on it, what it is accountable for and to whom it reports. Biographies, marketing plans and test scripts do not establish decision rights or accountability.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A board is clarifying its own role in technology oversight. Which activity is most appropriate for the board itself rather than delegated?
options: Configuring the firewall rules on the perimeter devices
Writing the code for the customer-facing mobile application
Approving the enterprise risk appetite and the strategic direction for IT
Resetting user passwords during the monthly maintenance window
items.explanation: The board sets direction and risk appetite, which are governance decisions. Firewall configuration, application coding and password resets are operational tasks that belong with management, not with the board.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A CIO is defining the contribution expected at the executive level. Which responsibility best fits the CIO role in enterprise governance?
options: Auditing the IT function and issuing independent assurance to the board
Translating business strategy into an IT agenda and reporting IT performance to the executive team
Personally approving every individual IT purchase request across the enterprise
Serving as the sole decision maker on all technology matters without peers
items.explanation: The CIO bridges business strategy and IT execution and reports performance to the executive team. Approving every purchase, acting without peers and performing independent audit confuse the CIO role with operational control or assurance.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: An enterprise is deciding where the security function should report. Which arrangement best supports independent security oversight?
options: The security leader reports at a level separate from the teams that build and run the systems
The security leader reports to the vendor that supplies the security products
The security leader has no reporting line and acts without any mandate
The security leader reports to the same manager who owns the production systems
items.explanation: Independence is supported when security oversight sits apart from those who build and operate the systems it reviews. Reporting into the same production owner, a product vendor or no one at all creates conflicts or an absence of authority.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: An enterprise is assigning data accountability. Which pairing correctly describes the roles?
options: The data owner is accountable for a data domain while stewards execute the day-to-day management
The data owner performs backups while the steward writes the security policy
The data owner and steward are always the same person by definition
The data owner approves audit reports while the steward issues them
items.explanation: In data governance the owner is accountable for a domain and its quality and use, while stewards carry out the operational management. Collapsing the roles, or confusing them with backup, policy authorship or audit, misstates the accountability model.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A governance review finds that one administrator can both change and approve production code. Which control principle is being violated?
options: Data minimization across the enterprise information holdings
Least functionality applied to the endpoint device configuration
Availability of the service during the agreed operating hours
Separation of duties between those who make changes and those who approve them
items.explanation: Separation of duties requires that the person who performs a sensitive action is not the same person who authorizes it. Data minimization, least functionality and availability are valid control objectives but do not describe the conflict between making and approving changes.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: An enterprise is assembling an IT steering committee that must balance business and technology perspectives. Which membership best achieves that balance?
options: Only the procurement officers who negotiate the contracts
Only junior developers who implement the changes
Senior business leaders together with the CIO and key IT managers
Only the external audit team that reviews the technology
items.explanation: Effective steering committees combine business leadership with technology leadership so that decisions weigh value and feasibility together. Membership limited to developers, auditors or procurement staff lacks the perspective the committee needs.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A board wants to understand how assurance over IT is organized. Under the three lines of defense model, which group provides independent assurance?
options: The risk and compliance function that supports management decisions
Internal audit, positioned outside the management and risk functions it reviews
The software vendor that supplies the monitoring product
The operational managers who own and run the technology processes
items.explanation: In the three lines model the first line owns and manages risk, the second supports and oversees it, and internal audit as the third line provides independent assurance. Operational owners, the risk function and vendors are not independent assurance providers.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A governance review finds tasks are completed but nobody can say who is accountable for outcomes. Which tool best clarifies this?
options: A network diagram showing the physical topology of the estate
A responsibility assignment matrix that names accountable and responsible parties
A purchase ledger listing all IT expenditure for the year
An incident log recording every service disruption
items.explanation: A responsibility assignment matrix maps activities to accountable and responsible parties, exposing gaps and duplication. Topology diagrams, ledgers and incident logs describe the environment but do not assign accountability for outcomes.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: An enterprise wants a coherent document set that ranges from high-level intent to step-by-step instructions. Which hierarchy is correct?
options: Policy states intent, standards set mandatory requirements and procedures describe how to comply
Procedures state intent, policies describe how to comply and standards are optional
Standards state intent, procedures are optional and policies describe the steps
Policy describes the steps, standards state intent and procedures are advisory
items.explanation: The accepted hierarchy is policy for intent, standards for mandatory requirements and procedures for the steps that achieve them. The other arrangements invert or misstate the purpose of each layer.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A business unit cannot meet a mandatory security standard before a deadline. Which governance response is most appropriate?
options: Delegate the decision to the vendor that supplies the affected system
Ignore the standard silently so the deadline can be met
Require a documented, time-bound exception with a compensating control and named owner
Change the standard for the whole enterprise to match the exception
items.explanation: Exceptions are legitimate when documented, time-bound, compensated and owned so the residual risk is known and revisited. Silent noncompliance, wholesale standard weakening and vendor-issued waivers all obscure accountability.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: An enterprise IT policies were written years ago and no longer reflect the environment. Which practice best keeps policies current?
options: Rewriting every policy annually regardless of whether anything changed
Scheduling periodic review with owners who confirm or update each policy
Letting staff edit policies whenever they see fit
Locking the documents so that no changes can be made
items.explanation: Periodic review with accountable owners keeps policies aligned to the changing environment and records the decision. Locking documents, calendar-driven rewriting with no analysis and uncontrolled editing each defeat the purpose of review.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A team is deciding whether a requirement belongs in a standard or a procedure. Which distinction is correct?
options: A standard sets a mandatory outcome while a procedure specifies the repeatable steps to achieve it
A standard is optional guidance while a procedure is legally binding
A standard describes the steps while a procedure states the intent
A standard and a procedure are interchangeable and may be used synonymously
items.explanation: Standards define mandatory requirements or outcomes, while procedures give the repeatable operational steps. Reversing them or treating the terms as synonyms blurs the difference between what must be achieved and how it is achieved.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: New IT policies have been approved but staff are unaware of them. Which action most improves policy awareness?
options: Filing the policies in a repository that no one visits
Publishing the policies once in a newsletter and assuming completion
Restricting the policies to the authors who drafted them
Delivering targeted communication and attestation so staff acknowledge the requirements
items.explanation: Awareness needs active, targeted communication and acknowledgment so the enterprise can show staff received and accepted the requirements. Silent filing, single-channel publication and restricted access all leave awareness unproven.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A governance function must know whether approved IT policies are actually followed. Which approach best provides that evidence?
options: Counting how many times the policy was downloaded from the repository
Measuring compliance against the policy on a recurring schedule and reporting exceptions
Assuming compliance because the policy was formally approved
Surveying staff once about whether they like the policy
items.explanation: Compliance is demonstrated by recurring measurement against the requirement with exceptions reported to owners. Approval alone, a popularity survey and download counts do not show whether the policy is being followed.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: An enterprise is building a data classification scheme. Which practice best supports consistent handling of information?
options: Defining classes with clear criteria and mapping controls to each class
Assigning classes informally and leaving handling entirely to individual judgment
Applying the highest controls to all data regardless of sensitivity
Classifying only the data that auditors ask to see
items.explanation: A usable classification scheme defines the classes and the criteria for each, then ties handling controls to the class. Auditing a subset, leaving handling to individual judgment or blanket-maximizing controls all fail to produce consistent, proportionate handling.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: An enterprise is issuing an acceptable use policy for technology. Which element is most important to include?
options: The full source code of every application in the estate
The personal home addresses of the IT staff
The vendor pricing schedule for the coming contract renewal
Permitted and prohibited uses together with the consequences of misuse
items.explanation: An acceptable use policy tells users what they may and may not do and what happens if they breach it. Source code, personal data and vendor pricing are unrelated to acceptable use and should not appear in such a policy.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A governance team wants to measure IT across several complementary perspectives. Which approach best accomplishes this?
options: A single financial ratio that reports IT cost as a percentage of revenue
A count of the number of IT staff who hold a certification
An IT balanced scorecard covering business contribution, user orientation, operational excellence and future orientation
A list of the oldest hardware assets awaiting replacement
items.explanation: The IT balanced scorecard assesses contribution to the business, user orientation, operational excellence and future readiness. A lone financial ratio, a certification count and an aging-asset list each capture only one narrow dimension.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A governance body wants indicators that reveal whether outcomes are being achieved rather than how much activity occurred. Which distinction applies?
options: Key goal indicators show whether goals are met while key performance indicators show progress toward them
The two terms are interchangeable and require no distinction
Key goal indicators count activity while key performance indicators set the strategy
Key performance indicators show outcomes while key goal indicators show effort
items.explanation: Key goal indicators lag and reveal whether an outcome was achieved, while key performance indicators lead and show progress toward the goal. Reversing them or treating them as synonyms removes the ability to distinguish outcome from effort.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: An executive wants a single view of IT performance against agreed targets. Which design best supports that view?
options: A narrative report with no numbers or targets
A list of software licenses approaching their expiry date
A raw export of every server event recorded in the last 24 hours
A dashboard showing each objective, its target, current status and trend
items.explanation: An executive dashboard ties each objective to its target, current value and trend so performance is quickly understood. Event exports, narratives without measures and license lists are data, not a performance view against targets.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: An enterprise wants to know whether its IT cost structure is competitive. Which approach is most suitable?
options: Comparing this year budget to last year without any external reference
Benchmarking comparable metrics against industry peers or standards
Asking the largest vendor whether the spend looks reasonable
Measuring only the electricity consumed by the data center
items.explanation: Benchmarking places the enterprise metrics against relevant peers or published standards to reveal relative position. Internal year-over-year comparison, a vendor opinion and a single utility measure cannot establish competitiveness.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A governance board is approving service level agreements for critical IT services. Which content is most important to govern?
options: Service targets, measurement methods, reporting cadence and remedies for breach
The personal career plans of the service delivery team
The architectural diagrams for a future system not yet funded
The marketing brochure used to advertise the service
items.explanation: Service level agreements are governed through defined targets, how they are measured, how often they are reported and what happens when they are missed. Career plans, unfunded designs and marketing material are not service level content.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A team has set IT performance targets that are always met with little effort. Which governance concern does this raise?
options: Meeting targets means governance oversight is unnecessary
The targets are too difficult and should be lowered further
The measurement method is irrelevant as long as targets are met
The targets may be too easy and may not drive meaningful improvement
items.explanation: Targets that are consistently trivial to meet fail to stretch performance or reveal risk. The concern is that they are too easy, not too hard, and measurement still matters while oversight remains necessary regardless of results.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A board is reviewing its IT reporting pack. Which change best improves its governance value?
options: Removing all risk information to keep the pack brief
Reporting only the IT budget and nothing about delivery or risk
Reporting outcomes, risks and trends against appetite rather than raw activity
Expanding the pack to include every operational log line produced
items.explanation: Boards govern best when reporting connects outcomes, risks and trends to the appetite they set. Log-level detail overwhelms, removing risk information removes governance content and reporting only budget hides delivery and risk entirely.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: An IT service level has breached its target for three consecutive months. Which governance action is most appropriate?
options: Adjust the target downward so the breach disappears
Stop reporting the metric to avoid concern
Require a root cause analysis with a corrective action plan owned by management
Blame the vendor publicly without any investigation
items.explanation: Persistent breaches call for root cause analysis and an owned corrective plan so the underlying problem is fixed. Lowering the target, hiding the metric or blaming a party without investigation addresses the symptom, not the cause.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A CFO asks how the enterprise should demonstrate that IT spending produced value. Which measure is most appropriate?
options: Reporting the total amount of money spent on technology
Relating investment outcomes to the business benefits they were approved to deliver
Counting the number of technology projects started
Listing the number of licenses purchased during the year
items.explanation: Value is demonstrated by comparing realized outcomes with the benefits the investment was approved to deliver. Total spend, project starts and license counts measure activity or cost, not the value produced.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A governance team is measuring the capability of a process. Which practice best produces a reliable rating?
options: Assessing defined attributes at each level and supporting the rating with evidence
Averaging the ratings of unrelated processes into one number
Asking the process owner for a number between one and five
Assuming the highest level because the process has documentation
items.explanation: Capability ratings are reliable when they assess defined attributes per level and are supported by evidence. A single self-assigned number, an assumption based on documentation and averaging unrelated processes all lack a defensible basis.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: A governance body wants assurance that IT practices conform to the adopted framework and internal policy. Which activity provides this?
options: An informal chat with staff about their preferred tools
A review of the framework publisher marketing materials
A brainstorming session about how the framework might be improved
A periodic conformance review that compares practice to the framework and policy
items.explanation: Conformance is established by periodically comparing actual practice against the framework and internal policy and reporting gaps. Brainstorming, informal chats and vendor marketing material cannot provide conformance evidence.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: An IT governance system was implemented last year and the enterprise wants it to keep improving. Which practice sustains improvement?
options: A one-time implementation that is then left untouched
An annual ceremony with no measurement or follow-up
A policy that forbids any change to the governance processes
A recurring cycle that measures performance, identifies gaps and acts on the findings
items.explanation: Governance systems improve through a repeating cycle of measure, identify gaps and act. One-time implementations, ceremonies without follow-up and change prohibitions all prevent the feedback loop that sustained improvement requires.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Governance of Enterprise IT

items.stem: An enterprise is planning the workforce needed to deliver its IT strategy. Which practice best ensures the right competencies are available?
options: Hiring only when a vacancy has existed for more than a year
Replacing all staff whenever a new technology is introduced
A skills inventory matched to future demand with a plan to close the gaps
Relying on the vendor to supply every skill the enterprise needs
items.explanation: Workforce planning compares current skills with future demand and defines how gaps will be closed through hire, train or source. Delayed hiring, wholesale replacement and complete vendor reliance leave demand and supply mismatched.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: A key IT specialist is leaving and much of the knowledge is undocumented. Which action best mitigates the resource risk?
options: Use cross-training and documentation to transfer knowledge before departure
Outsource the entire function without a knowledge transfer step
Allow the knowledge to leave and hope the risk never materializes
Delete the specialist accounts immediately without any handover
items.explanation: Knowledge resource risk is mitigated by transferring expertise through cross-training and documentation before the individual departs. Letting it go, abrupt account removal and outsourcing without handover all increase the risk instead of reducing it.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: An enterprise has a single person holding critical operational knowledge. Which governance action best reduces the key-person dependency?
options: Remove the documentation so that only one person can perform the work
Postpone any planning until the person announces a resignation
Increase that person salary and take no other action
Identify a successor and document the critical processes for continuity
items.explanation: Key-person risk falls when a successor is identified and critical processes are documented so continuity does not depend on one individual. Pay alone, hiding documentation and waiting for a resignation all leave the dependency in place.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: An enterprise observes repeated security mistakes by staff despite having policies. Which response best addresses the underlying IT resource issue?
options: Repeat the policy document to staff without any training activity
Discipline staff without understanding why the mistakes occur
Deliver role-appropriate training and measure whether behaviour improved
Ignore the errors because the policy was already communicated
items.explanation: The resource gap is a competency gap, so role-appropriate training with measured behavioural change is the appropriate response. Re-stating policy, punitive action without analysis and ignoring the errors do not build the capability that prevents recurrence.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: An enterprise is defining accountability for an IT service that spans several teams. Which approach best prevents ownership gaps?
options: Assign no owner because several teams are involved
Assign a single accountable owner for the service across all contributing teams
Assign ownership to whichever team happens to be on shift
Assign ownership to the vendor with no internal counterpart
items.explanation: Cross-team services need one accountable owner even when many teams contribute, so gaps and conflicts can be resolved. No owner, shift-based ownership and unmanaged vendor ownership each create the gaps the enterprise is trying to avoid.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: An enterprise is reviewing the productivity of its IT workforce. Which metric best reflects capability rather than mere activity?
options: The count of tickets opened regardless of resolution
The number of emails sent by each team member
The number of hours each employee spends in meetings
The proportion of planned work delivered to the agreed scope and quality
items.explanation: Capability is shown by delivering planned work to scope and quality, not by activity volume. Emails, meeting hours and ticket counts measure effort or load and can rise even when delivery does not improve.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: An enterprise wants its technology staff to raise risks early rather than hide them. Which governance action best supports this behaviour?
options: Require staff to certify that no problems exist
Discourage communication between IT and the business
Create a culture where raising concerns is expected and not punished
Sanction anyone who reports a problem in their own area
items.explanation: Early risk disclosure depends on a culture that rewards and protects raising concerns. Punishing reporters, demanding declarations of perfection and blocking communication all suppress the information governance needs.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: An enterprise is preparing its IT budget. Which approach best aligns funding with strategy?
options: Fund each department equally regardless of demand or value
Fund initiatives according to their strategic priority and expected benefit
Carry forward last year budget without any review
Fund only the projects with the lowest estimated cost
items.explanation: Strategic budgeting directs funds to the initiatives that matter most and are expected to deliver benefit. Equal allocation, unreviewed carry-forward and cheapest-first selection ignore priority and value.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: A governance board must distinguish spending that creates capability from spending that keeps the lights on. Which classification is correct?
options: Capital and growth investment versus ongoing operational run cost
Approved and unapproved spending
Domestic and foreign expenditure
Hardware and software spending
items.explanation: The governance distinction is between investment that changes capability, such as capital and growth, and operational cost that sustains current services. Approval status, geography and asset category do not separate capability building from run cost.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: Business units complain that IT costs are opaque. Which practice best improves transparency?
options: Billing each business unit the same flat fee regardless of usage
Reporting only a single enterprise-wide IT total each year
Showback or chargeback that attributes costs to the services and consumers they support
Hiding the cost breakdown to avoid difficult conversations
items.explanation: Transparency comes from attributing costs to the services consumed so demand can be understood and managed. A single total, concealed detail and flat fees all obscure the relationship between consumption and cost.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: An enterprise is comparing the lifetime cost of two technology options. Which measure best supports the comparison?
options: The vendor advertised discount at the point of sale
Total cost of ownership across acquisition, operation, support and retirement
The number of features listed in the product datasheet
The purchase price alone for each option
items.explanation: Total cost of ownership captures acquisition, operation, support and disposal so options are compared on their full economic impact. Purchase price, sales discounts and feature counts each omit major cost components.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: An enterprise struggles to fund innovation because all IT funds are consumed by run cost. Which governance decision best rebalances spending?
options: Continue funding only run cost and expect innovation to be free
Cut all run spending to zero to fund every proposed project
Borrow against future budgets to fund daily operations
Protect a defined share of the budget for change and innovation
items.explanation: A deliberate allocation for change protects innovation from being crowded out by run cost. Funding run cost alone starves change, eliminating run funding is unsustainable and borrowing for operations compounds the imbalance.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: A finance committee wants IT investment proposals to be comparable. Which requirement best achieves this?
options: Every proposal uses a different template chosen by its author
Every proposal omits costs so the benefits look larger
Every proposal states its costs, expected benefits and risks on a consistent basis
Every proposal relies on the vendor own return estimate
items.explanation: Comparability requires a consistent method covering costs, benefits and risks so proposals can be weighed against one another. Varied templates, omitted costs and vendor-authored returns prevent fair comparison.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: An enterprise is planning infrastructure capacity for expected growth. Which practice best avoids both outages and waste?
options: Assume demand will never change and take no action
Forecast demand from business plans and provision to meet it with a defined margin
Buy the maximum capacity available regardless of need
Provision only for current load and ignore the business forecast
items.explanation: Capacity planning balances the business forecast against provisioned capacity with a deliberate margin. Buying maximum capacity wastes resources while ignoring forecasts or assuming no change risks outages.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: An enterprise cannot say which infrastructure assets it owns or where they are. Which practice best establishes control?
options: Maintain an accurate asset inventory with ownership, location and lifecycle status
Rely on the vendor record with no internal inventory
Count only the assets that are currently faulty
Guess the asset count from the procurement budget
items.explanation: Control over infrastructure begins with an accurate inventory recording ownership, location and lifecycle. Budget estimates, vendor-only records and fault-only counts leave the estate unknown and unmanaged.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: An enterprise supports many incompatible versions of the same platform. Which governance action best reduces this complexity?
options: Define a supported standard and a plan to retire nonconforming versions
Allow every team to choose any version indefinitely
Standardize on the oldest version to avoid any migration
Add more versions to accommodate every new preference
items.explanation: Reducing complexity requires an agreed supported standard plus a retirement path for nonconforming versions. Unlimited choice, oldest-only standardization and adding versions each increase rather than reduce the estate complexity.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: A critical service depends on a single data center with no redundancy. Which action best addresses the infrastructure resource risk?
options: Accept the risk and document it without any mitigation
Increase the marketing for the service to offset outages
Move the service to an unknown location without planning
Introduce redundancy or failover so the service survives a site loss
items.explanation: Single-site dependence is a resilience gap best closed by redundancy or failover so a site loss does not stop the service. Accepting without mitigation, marketing around outages and unplanned relocation do not reduce the risk.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: An enterprise is moving workloads to the cloud. Which governance consideration is most important before migration?
options: Assuming the provider owns all compliance obligations
Selecting the provider that advertises the lowest headline price
Understanding data residency, security, exit and integration obligations
Migrating every workload at once without any assessment
items.explanation: Cloud governance requires explicit understanding of residency, security, exit and integration obligations. Cheapest headline price, undifferentiated migration and assuming the provider carries compliance all leave critical risks unmanaged.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: An enterprise is running infrastructure that the vendor no longer supports. Which governance action is most appropriate?
options: Ignore the risk until an incident forces action
Assess the risk and plan a funded upgrade or replacement
Remove the asset from the inventory to avoid attention
Continue running it indefinitely because it still works
items.explanation: Unsupported infrastructure carries elevated security and availability risk, so it should be assessed and remediated through a funded plan. Running it on, waiting for an incident or hiding it from the inventory increases rather than manages the exposure.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: Business decisions are based on reports whose data is often wrong. Which practice best improves the information resource?
options: Ignore the errors because the reports look professional
Define data quality dimensions and measure them with owners for each domain
Delete the reports to avoid using bad data
Ask users to correct every error manually without addressing causes
items.explanation: Information quality improves when dimensions such as accuracy and completeness are defined, measured and owned by domain. Ignoring errors, deleting reports and manual correction without root cause leave the underlying quality unmanaged.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: An enterprise keeps every record forever with no disposal. Which governance practice best manages the information resource?
options: Apply a retention schedule with secure disposal when the period ends
Retain all information indefinitely to avoid any decision
Delete records randomly without any schedule
Let each employee decide retention based on personal preference
items.explanation: A retention schedule sets how long each class is kept and triggers secure disposal, balancing legal and business needs. Indefinite retention, random deletion and personal preference all fail to manage the information lifecycle.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: Staff report they cannot find the information they need to do their work. Which practice best improves accessibility?
options: Duplicate information into every possible location
Store all information in personal folders with no index
Organize information with clear ownership, metadata and search so it can be found
Restrict access so broadly that no one can retrieve anything
items.explanation: Accessibility depends on ownership, meaningful metadata and effective search so information can be located and trusted. Personal unindexed storage, excessive restriction and uncontrolled duplication all obstruct retrieval.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: An enterprise wants controls applied in proportion to the sensitivity of information. Which practice best achieves this?
options: Apply controls only to information that customers can see
Classify information and apply controls appropriate to each classification
Leave classification to the discretion of whoever creates the information
Apply the same controls to all information regardless of sensitivity
items.explanation: Proportionate protection follows classification, with controls matched to each level. Uniform controls overprotect the trivial and may underprotect the sensitive, customer-only scope misses internal data and unmanaged discretion produces inconsistency.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: An enterprise loses expertise whenever staff leave because nothing is recorded. Which practice best preserves knowledge as a resource?
options: Maintain a knowledge base with contribution and review responsibilities
Rely solely on the memories of current staff
Store knowledge only in private email mailboxes
Discourage documentation to speed up daily work
items.explanation: Knowledge is preserved when it is captured in a maintained base with named contributors and reviewers. Reliance on memory, private mailboxes and discouraging documentation all leave knowledge fragile and inaccessible.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: An enterprise is deciding which IT services to source externally. Which factor is most important to that decision?
options: The vendor sales representative personal rapport
The proximity of the vendor office to the enterprise
The colour scheme of the vendor proposal document
Whether the service is strategic and how well the risk can be managed
items.explanation: Sourcing decisions weigh strategic importance and the enterprise ability to manage the associated risk. Personal rapport, office proximity and proposal aesthetics are not substantive criteria for outsourcing a service.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: An enterprise is selecting a vendor for a critical service. Which practice best supports a defensible decision?
options: Award the contract based on a single unstructured meeting
Evaluate candidates against documented criteria including capability, risk and cost
Choose the first vendor that responds to the request
Select the vendor that spends the most on marketing
items.explanation: A defensible selection uses documented criteria covering capability, risk and cost so the choice can be explained and reviewed. First response, marketing spend and a lone meeting are not fair or repeatable selection methods.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: A service provider consistently misses the agreed service levels. Which governance action is most appropriate?
options: Hold a formal review against the contract and require a corrective plan
Ignore the misses to preserve a friendly relationship
Stop measuring service levels so the misses are not visible
Renew the contract automatically without any review
items.explanation: Vendor performance should be managed through a formal contract review and an owned corrective plan with remedies. Automatic renewal, ignoring the misses and ceasing measurement all let underperformance persist unaddressed.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: An enterprise relies on a vendor that has poor security practices. Which practice best manages the third-party resource risk?
options: Assume the vendor reputation guarantees adequate security
Move more critical data to the vendor without any assessment
Ignore the practices because the contract is already signed
Assess the vendor controls and require remediation or a compensating control
items.explanation: Third-party risk is managed by assessing the vendor controls and requiring remediation or compensation. Reputation alone, expanding data sharing and ignoring the issue after contracting all leave the exposure in place.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: An enterprise finds that several systems overlap and duplicate costs. Which practice best optimizes the IT resource base?
options: Keep every system because each has at least one user
Duplicate functionality further so each team is self-sufficient
Review the portfolio to consolidate or retire redundant capability
Ignore overlaps because they are hard to measure
items.explanation: Optimization finds and removes redundancy so resources are used efficiently. Keeping every system, adding duplication and ignoring overlaps all increase cost and complexity without improving capability.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: An enterprise is considering ending an outsourcing arrangement. Which governance consideration is most important?
options: The ability to exit with data, knowledge and service continuity intact
The distance between the two organization offices
The vendor wish to keep the contract active
The number of years the relationship has lasted
items.explanation: Exit planning must ensure the enterprise can leave with its data, knowledge and uninterrupted service. The vendor preferences, relationship duration and physical distance are not the factors that determine whether an exit is safe.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - IT Resources

items.stem: An enterprise is preparing a business case for a major IT investment. Which element is most essential?
options: A promise of benefits with no measurement approach
A vendor brochure presented as the analysis
A description of the technology that omits the expected outcomes
A clear statement of expected benefits, costs, risks and how benefits will be measured
items.explanation: A sound business case states the expected benefits, costs and risks and how the benefits will be measured so realization can later be tested. Omitting outcomes, promising without measurement and using a brochure as analysis all prevent accountability for value.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Benefits Realization

items.stem: A governance board wants to know whether an IT investment is delivering the intended value. Which practice best provides that assurance?
options: Counting how much was spent on the investment
Comparing realized benefits with the benefits in the approved business case
Measuring how many people use the system
Confirming the project finished on schedule
items.explanation: Value delivery is confirmed by comparing realized benefits against those promised in the approved case. Spend, user counts and schedule adherence are relevant inputs but do not by themselves show that the intended value was achieved.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Benefits Realization

items.stem: An enterprise approves an investment without defining who will realize the benefits. Which action best corrects this gap?
options: Assign benefit owners and define the realization plan before approval
Assume the IT department will realize all benefits automatically
Wait until the project closes and then assign owners
Declare the benefits unrealizable and cancel the investment
items.explanation: Benefits are realized when owners are named and a plan defines how and when each benefit will be achieved, ideally before approval. Automatic assumptions, delayed assignment and premature cancellation all undermine realization.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Benefits Realization

items.stem: A benefits review finds that reported benefits cannot be verified. Which practice best restores credibility?
options: Drop the measurement of benefits altogether
Accept the sponsor unaudited claims as evidence
Report only the benefits that are easy to count
Define metrics with a baseline and a measurement method for each benefit
items.explanation: Verifiable benefits require agreed metrics with a baseline and a documented measurement method. Unaudited claims, selective reporting and abandoning measurement all remove the evidence that makes realization credible.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Benefits Realization

items.stem: An enterprise repeatedly invests in IT without seeing the promised returns. Which governance root cause is most likely?
options: Excessive documentation during the project
A preference for open-source components
Weak benefit ownership and oversight across the investment lifecycle
Too few vendors competing for the work
items.explanation: Persistent failure to realize returns usually reflects weak ownership and oversight of benefits through the lifecycle. Vendor counts, documentation levels and open-source preferences are unrelated to whether the enterprise manages benefits to realization.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Benefits Realization

items.stem: A project scope has changed significantly since the business case was approved. Which governance response is most appropriate?
options: Proceed without review because the original case was once approved
Cancel the project immediately without any assessment
Reassess and reapprove the business case against the changed scope and benefits
Ignore the change and report the original benefits as achieved
items.explanation: Material scope change invalidates the original analysis, so the case must be reassessed and reapproved. Proceeding on a stale approval, cancelling reflexively or misreporting the original benefits all breach sound investment governance.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Benefits Realization

items.stem: A governance board is reviewing its portfolio of IT investments. Which practice best optimizes portfolio value?
options: Funding projects strictly in the order they were proposed
Balancing investments across risk, return and strategic contribution
Selecting only the projects with the largest budgets
Rejecting every project that carries any uncertainty
items.explanation: Portfolio value is optimized by balancing risk, return and strategic contribution across the whole set of investments. Proposal order, budget size and blanket rejection of uncertainty are not portfolio optimization criteria.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Benefits Realization

items.stem: An enterprise finishes IT projects but never checks whether benefits arrived. Which practice best closes this loop?
options: Track benefits after go-live until they are realized or shown to be unattainable
Delegate all benefit tracking to the vendor
Close the project as soon as the technology is deployed
Assume benefits arrive once the system is live
items.explanation: Benefits realization continues after deployment through tracking until the benefit is achieved or shown unattainable. Closing at deployment, assuming arrival and delegating tracking to the vendor leave realization unverified.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Benefits Realization

items.stem: An executive asks how to articulate the value of IT beyond cost reduction. Which framing is most complete?
options: Value cannot be articulated and should not be attempted
Value is the number of technology components deployed
Value is only ever measured as cost reduction
Value includes revenue enablement, risk reduction, compliance and service improvement as well as cost
items.explanation: IT value spans revenue enablement, risk reduction, compliance, service improvement and cost so it should be described across these dimensions. Reducing value to cost alone, refusing to articulate it or counting components each misrepresent the contribution.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Benefits Realization

items.stem: A project delivered its technology but the business did not change its processes. Which concept best explains the missing benefit?
options: Technology alone always guarantees the intended benefit
Benefits are unrelated to process change
The benefit was never real and should be ignored
Benefits often depend on business changes outside the technology delivery
items.explanation: Many benefits depend on complementary business changes such as process redesign and adoption, so technology delivery alone may not realize them. Assuming technology guarantees benefit, ignoring process change or dismissing the benefit misreads the dependency.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Benefits Realization

items.stem: A governance board wants to stop weak investments before more money is spent. Which practice best accomplishes this?
options: Release the entire budget at the start and never review again
Review investments only after they are fully completed
Use staged funding gates that review benefits and risk before releasing more funds
Approve investments without any defined criteria
items.explanation: Staged gates review benefits and risk before further funds are released, allowing weak investments to be stopped early. Upfront full funding, post-completion review and criteria-free approval all remove the opportunity to intervene.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Benefits Realization

items.stem: A benefit is promised to the business but the business sponsor is passive. Which action best improves the chance of realization?
options: Engage the sponsor actively as the accountable owner of the benefit
Remove the benefit from the business case
Transfer benefit accountability to the vendor
Ignore the sponsor and let the project team decide
items.explanation: Benefits tied to business outcomes need an engaged, accountable business owner to drive realization. Shifting accountability to a vendor, bypassing the sponsor or deleting the benefit all remove the ownership that realization requires.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Benefits Realization

items.stem: A board is defining its risk appetite for technology. What does risk appetite express?
options: The budget available to buy security products
The number of vulnerabilities found in the last scan
The list of risks that have already caused an incident
The amount and type of risk the enterprise is willing to accept in pursuit of its objectives
items.explanation: Risk appetite is the amount and type of risk the enterprise is willing to pursue or retain in pursuit of its objectives. Incident lists, security budgets and scan counts are inputs or outputs but do not define appetite.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: A governance team is distinguishing risk appetite from risk tolerance. Which statement is correct?
options: Appetite applies only to financial risk while tolerance applies only to IT risk
The two terms are identical and may be used interchangeably
Appetite is the broad level of risk accepted while tolerance is the acceptable variation around a specific objective
Tolerance is set by the vendor while appetite is set by the auditor
items.explanation: Appetite sets the broad level of risk the enterprise will accept, while tolerance is the acceptable deviation from a specific objective or metric. Treating them as identical or assigning them to a vendor or auditor misstates who sets them.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: An enterprise is assessing how much risk it could bear before failing. Which concept describes that limit?
options: Risk appetite, the risk the enterprise prefers to take
Risk capacity, the maximum risk the enterprise can absorb
Risk register, the list of identified risks
Risk treatment, the response chosen for a risk
items.explanation: Risk capacity is the maximum risk the enterprise can absorb before its objectives or viability are threatened. Appetite is the preferred level, the register lists risks and treatment is the response, none of which describe the absolute limit.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: An enterprise is drafting a risk appetite statement for technology. Which characteristic makes it usable for decisions?
options: It changes every day according to the latest incident
It lists aspirations without any boundaries or limits
It is written only for the audit committee and hidden from management
It states qualitative boundaries and, where possible, quantitative limits
items.explanation: A usable appetite statement gives qualitative boundaries and quantitative limits so decisions can be tested against it. Statements without limits cannot guide choices, hidden statements cannot be applied and daily change makes it unusable as a reference.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: A business unit wants to accept a risk that exceeds the enterprise stated appetite. Which governance response is correct?
options: Assume the appetite can be ignored when a unit finds it inconvenient
Delegate the appetite decision to the affected vendor
Escalate the decision for explicit approval at the level that owns the appetite
Allow the business unit to accept it silently without any record
items.explanation: Decisions that exceed the stated appetite must be escalated to the level accountable for setting and accepting that appetite so the risk is explicitly owned. Silent acceptance, treating appetite as optional and vendor delegation all bypass proper risk governance.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: An enterprise is establishing a technology risk management framework. Which sequence best describes a standard risk process?
options: Buy tools, scan systems, ignore findings and repeat
Identify, analyze, evaluate, treat and monitor risks
Insure everything, close the register and stop reviewing
Delegate all risk activity to the vendor without oversight
items.explanation: A standard risk process identifies, analyzes, evaluates, treats and then monitors risks in a continuing cycle. Tool-driven scanning without action, insurance-only approaches and unmanaged vendor delegation are not a framework.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: An enterprise manages technology risk separately from enterprise risk. Which improvement best aligns the two?
options: Integrate technology risk into the enterprise risk management framework and reporting
Keep technology risk entirely isolated from enterprise risk discussions
Report technology risk only to the IT department
Exclude technology risk from board reporting altogether
items.explanation: Technology risk should be integrated into enterprise risk management and reporting so it is considered alongside other risks. Isolation, IT-only reporting and exclusion from the board all fragment the risk picture the board needs.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: A governance body is defining who owns technology risk decisions. Which arrangement best reflects sound risk governance?
options: No one owns risk because it is unavoidable
Risk ownership rests solely with the external auditor
Risk ownership rests with business and process owners, with independent oversight by risk and audit functions
Risk ownership rests solely with the technology vendor
items.explanation: Sound risk governance places ownership with the business and process owners who carry the risk, with independent oversight from risk and audit. Auditor-only or vendor-only ownership and disclaiming all ownership are not accountable arrangements.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: An enterprise cannot consistently decide which risks matter most. Which practice best resolves this?
options: Treat all risks as equally serious regardless of impact
Define risk criteria and scales so likelihood and impact are rated consistently
Rank risks by the order they were discovered
Rate each risk by the intuition of whoever is available
items.explanation: Consistent prioritization comes from agreed criteria and rating scales for likelihood and impact. Intuition, treating all risks alike and discovery order all produce inconsistent and indefensible prioritization.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: An enterprise is identifying technology risks for a new service. Which technique best broadens the identification?
options: Structured workshops with business and technical stakeholders covering the service end to end
A single person listing whatever comes to mind
Reviewing only the risks from a different unrelated service
Waiting for an incident to reveal the risks
items.explanation: Structured, cross-functional workshops over the full service lifecycle surface risks that one person or an unrelated review would miss. Waiting for an incident identifies risk only after harm has occurred.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: A team is estimating how likely a risk event is to occur. Which basis is most defensible?
options: A guess made without any supporting information
The personal fear level of the person assessing the risk
The order in which the risk appears in the register
Evidence such as historical incidents, control effectiveness and threat data
items.explanation: Likelihood estimates are defensible when grounded in evidence such as incident history, control effectiveness and threat data. Guesses, personal fear and register order have no analytical basis.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: An enterprise is assessing the impact of a technology risk. Which approach best captures the full consequence?
options: Consider no impacts because they are hard to quantify
Consider only the direct cost of replacing hardware
Consider financial, operational, legal, reputational and strategic consequences
Consider only the impact on the IT department workload
items.explanation: Impact assessment should span financial, operational, legal, reputational and strategic consequences. Hardware cost alone, IT workload alone and declining to assess impact all understate the true consequence of a risk.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: A risk is rated after existing controls are considered. Which term describes that rating?
options: Risk appetite, the level the enterprise prefers to accept
Residual risk, the risk remaining after controls are applied
Risk capacity, the maximum the enterprise can absorb
Inherent risk, the risk before any controls are considered
items.explanation: Residual risk is what remains after existing controls are taken into account, whereas inherent risk is assessed before controls. Appetite is the preferred level and capacity the maximum absorbable level, so neither describes the post-control rating.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: A governance body wants to understand overall technology exposure. Which practice best supports this?
options: Report each risk in isolation with no aggregation
Report only the single largest risk and ignore the rest
Hide the smaller risks so the picture looks simpler
Aggregate individual risks to show concentration and total exposure by category
items.explanation: Aggregation reveals concentration and total exposure that isolated risks hide, which is what a governance body needs for oversight. Isolation, single-risk reporting and hiding smaller risks all distort the overall picture.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: An enterprise wants to express risk in monetary terms. Which approach is most appropriate?
options: Assign every risk the same arbitrary monetary value
Refuse to quantify any risk regardless of available data
Estimate the potential loss and its likelihood using available data and assumptions
Use the vendor estimate as the only input
items.explanation: Quantification estimates potential loss and likelihood from available data with documented assumptions. Uniform arbitrary values, blanket refusal and sole reliance on a vendor estimate are not credible quantification methods.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: A governance team is choosing a response to an identified risk. Which set best describes the treatment options?
options: Hire, train, retain and retire the staff involved
Avoid, mitigate, transfer and accept the risk
Identify, analyze, evaluate and monitor the risk
Plan, build, run and monitor the response
items.explanation: Risk treatment options are avoid, mitigate, transfer and accept. The other sets describe the risk process itself, the management cycle or a workforce sequence, none of which are treatment choices.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: An enterprise decides to reduce a risk by adding a control. Which consideration is most important?
options: Whether the control reduces the risk to within the enterprise appetite cost-effectively
Whether the control is the newest product on the market
Whether the control adds complexity without reducing risk
Whether the control is the most expensive available
items.explanation: Mitigation should bring the risk within appetite at a proportionate cost, which is the test of a good control. Cost alone, novelty alone and complexity without risk reduction do not justify the control.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: An enterprise buys insurance against a technology risk. Which statement about the treatment is correct?
options: Transfer eliminates the risk entirely and removes all responsibility
Transfer is identical to avoiding the risk
Transfer shifts the financial consequence but not accountability for the risk
Transfer means the insurer now owns the enterprise risk decisions
items.explanation: Transfer such as insurance shifts the financial impact to another party but the enterprise remains accountable for managing and disclosing the risk. It does not eliminate the risk, equal avoidance or transfer ownership of decisions.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: An enterprise decides to accept a residual risk. Which condition makes acceptance defensible?
options: The risk is ignored because no one noticed it
The risk is within appetite and the acceptance is explicitly approved and documented
The risk is accepted by a junior employee without authority
The risk exceeds appetite but is accepted silently
items.explanation: Acceptance is defensible when the risk is within the agreed appetite and is explicitly approved and documented. Oversight, unauthorized acceptance and silent acceptance of a risk beyond appetite are not sound decisions.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: A risk treatment plan has been agreed but no one is driving it. Which action best ensures the plan progresses?
options: Archive the plan and remove it from tracking
Assign a named owner with authority, resources and a due date
Leave the plan open with no owner and hope it completes
Assume the last person to discuss the risk will act
