items.explanation: Treatment progresses when a named owner has the authority, resources and deadline to act. Ownerless plans, diffuse assumptions and archiving before completion all leave the risk untreated.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: An enterprise treats a risk and then never revisits it. Which practice best maintains oversight?
options: Monitor key risk indicators and review the risk on a defined cadence
Close the risk register after the first treatment
Stop measuring once a control is implemented
Assume the risk stays at the same level forever
items.explanation: Risk levels change, so monitoring through key risk indicators and scheduled review keeps oversight current. Assuming stasis, closing the register and stopping measurement all leave the enterprise unaware of changes.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: A board wants risk reports that support decision making. Which content best serves that purpose?
options: An exhaustive list of every risk with no prioritization
Only risks that have already caused a loss
A narrative that omits the level of each risk
Significant risks with trend, exposure against appetite and treatment status
items.explanation: Decision-ready reporting highlights significant risks with trend, exposure relative to appetite and treatment status. Exhaustive unprioritized lists, loss-only reporting and narratives without levels all obscure what the board must decide.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: An enterprise wants advance warning that a technology risk is rising. Which measure best provides it?
options: Lagging indicators that only record harm after it occurs
The number of meetings held about the risk
Leading indicators that move before the risk materializes
The age of the risk entry in the register
items.explanation: Leading indicators signal that exposure is increasing before the risk event occurs, which enables preventive action. Lagging indicators record harm too late, while meeting counts and entry age do not measure exposure.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: A key risk indicator crosses its defined threshold. Which governance response is most appropriate?
options: Record the breach but take no action
Wait until the risk causes an incident before acting
Trigger the escalation path and require an owner response
Raise the threshold so the breach disappears
items.explanation: A breached threshold should trigger the predefined escalation and an owner response so the exposure is addressed. Waiting for an incident, moving the threshold and recording without action all defeat the purpose of monitoring.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: An enterprise is conducting a business impact analysis. Which output is most essential?
options: The marketing budget for the coming year
The critical processes and their recovery priorities and dependencies
A copy of the vendor product catalogue
A list of employees who prefer to work remotely
items.explanation: A business impact analysis identifies critical processes, their recovery priorities and dependencies so continuity can be planned. Remote-work preferences, marketing budgets and vendor catalogues are unrelated to business impact.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: A continuity team is setting recovery objectives for a critical system. Which pairing is correct?
options: Recovery time objective is the target time to restore service and recovery point objective is the acceptable data loss
Recovery time objective is the acceptable data loss and recovery point objective is the target restore time
Both objectives measure the cost of the recovery effort
Both objectives are set by the vendor without business input
items.explanation: Recovery time objective is the target elapsed time to restore service, and recovery point objective is the acceptable amount of data loss. Reversing them, treating both as cost or setting them without business input misstates their meaning.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: An enterprise has a continuity plan that has never been tested. Which practice best validates it?
options: Assume the plan works because it is well written
Store the plan securely and never review it
Test only the portions that are cheap to test
Exercise the plan through scenarios and act on the lessons learned
items.explanation: Plans are validated by exercising them against realistic scenarios and improving them from the lessons. Assuming effectiveness, never reviewing and testing only cheap portions leave the plan real readiness unknown.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: An enterprise continuity strategy relies on a backup site that has never been verified. Which action best addresses the risk?
options: Document the site without testing its capacity
Assume the site will work when it is needed
Remove the backup site to reduce cost
Verify the backup site can actually support the recovery objectives
items.explanation: A recovery site must be verified to actually meet the recovery time and point objectives before it is relied upon. Assumption, removal and documentation without testing all leave continuity dependent on an unproven capability.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: An enterprise continuity plan ignores key suppliers on whom a critical process depends. Which improvement is most important?
options: Remove suppliers from the process design to avoid the dependency
Ignore supplier dependencies because they are external
Identify and plan for critical supplier dependencies in the continuity strategy
Assume suppliers will recover at the same time as the enterprise
items.explanation: Critical supplier dependencies must be identified and planned for so continuity covers the whole process rather than only internal systems. Assuming synchronized recovery, redesigning to dodge the dependency and ignoring external dependencies all leave the process exposed.
items.reference: ISACA CGEIT Exam Content Outline - Risk Optimization

items.stem: An enterprise develops its technology recovery plan separately from its business continuity plan. Which change best improves resilience?
options: Keep the plans separate so neither team has to coordinate
Treat the technology plan as a substitute for the business plan
Integrate the technology recovery plan with the business continuity plan around shared priorities
Discard the business continuity plan and rely on backups
items.explanation: Resilience improves when technology recovery and business continuity plans are integrated around the same process priorities. Keeping them apart, substituting one for the other or discarding the business plan all create gaps between technical recovery and business need.
